'''''Cistus libanotis''''' is a [[shrub]]by [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Cistaceae]], with white flowers. It has been confused with ''[[Cistus clusii]]'', which it resembles, resulting in some uncertainty in its distribution. It is [[endemic]] to the [[Iberian Peninsula]] (in southern [[Portugal]] and southwestern [[Spain]]).

==Description==
''Cistus libanotis'' is a prostrate or less often erect [[shrub]], up to {{convert|80|–|120|cm|ftin|abbr=on|0}} tall. It leaves are dark green, long and thin in shape, usually {{convert|2|–|4|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} long by {{convert|2|–|5|mm|in|abbr=on|2}} wide and with turned under (revolute) margins. The upper surfaces of the leaves have only a few stellate hairs, particularly on the margins and the veins; the lower surfaces have a conspicuous vein and two dense bands of short stellate hairs. The flowers are arranged in [[cyme (botany)|cyme]]s or whorls, the top group forming an [[umbel]] of three or four flowers. Each flower has three striped reddish [[sepal]]s, {{convert|7|–|9|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} long by {{convert|4|–|5|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} wide, and five white [[petal]]s with a yellow spot at the base, {{convert|10|–|13|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} long by {{convert|9|–|12|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} wide. The [[stamen]]s are unequal in length, longer than the [[pistil]]. The [[Style (botany)|style]] is short. The fruiting capsule is {{convert|6|–|7|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} long, with relatively large seeds up to {{convert|1.8|mm|in|abbr=on|2}} in diameter.<ref name=DemoMont93/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Cistus libanotis'' is native to the southwestern [[Iberian Peninsula]] (southern [[Portugal]] and south-west [[Spain]]) where it is commonly found in dry, sandy coastal areas from [[Campo de Gibraltar]] to [[Cape St. Vincent]] and between [[Alcácer do Sal]] and [[Grândola]], but it can also be found as far inland as [[Paradas, Seville]].<ref name=Warb68/><ref name=GuzmLled09/><ref>{{cite web |title=Cistus |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/03_066_01_Cistus.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=24 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cistus libanotis L. |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1Cistus+libanotis |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=24 November 2020}}</ref> There are records of this species in [[Morocco]], [[Algeria]] and [[Tunisia]],<ref name=GuzmLled09/> although these may belong to ''Cistus libanotis'' <small>[[Auctorum|auct.]] non L.</small>, i.e. ''[[Cistus clusii|C. clusii]]''.<ref name=CiveLeclDemoAgna11/><ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" />

==Taxonomy==
''Cistus libanotis'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1759.<ref name=TPL_kew-2723492/> A different but similar species, ''[[Cistus clusii]]'', has regularly been mis-identified as this species.<ref name=Warb68/> A 2011 [[Molecular phylogenetics|molecular phylogenetic study]] placed ''C. libanotis'' in the [[Cistus#Phylogeny|white and whitish pink clade]] of ''Cistus'' species. No strong relationship with ''C. clusii'' was found.<ref name=CiveLeclDemoAgna11/>

The specific epithet ''libanotis'' was the word used for [[Rosmarinus officinalis|rosemary]] by [[Pliny the Elder|Pliny]].<ref name=JMLED/>

==Phylogeny==
''Cistus libanotis'' belongs to the white and whitish pink flowered clade of ''Cistus'' species.
